chunks: And Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd al-Minqarī narrated from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muḥammad, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, or I heard him say: “A free woman is not compelled to breastfeed the child, but an Umm al-Walad is compelled.”

key_terms.أُمُّ الْوَلَدِ: a female slave who bore her master a child
key_terms.الْحُرَّةُ: a free woman, as distinguished from a bondwoman

ai.seo_question: Is a mother legally compelled to breastfeed her child in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning breastfeeding obligations. It distinguishes between a free woman and an Umm al-Walad, stating that the free woman is not compelled to nurse the child, whereas the Umm al-Walad is compelled.
